correctness.rationale: For each fixed -1<b<0, the unperturbed period-two Jacobian product has trace 4b²-2 (strictly between -2 and 2), determinant 1, and no +1 eigenvalue; hence analytic continuation of the two-cycle is valid. The unit-determinant condition has nonzero derivative 8 with respect to mean drive a, permitting a unique analytic spectral crossing. Exact midpoint/difference identities reduce the two-cycle and determinant to a quadratic radical in the mean phase q. The q² coefficients yield a2=(b+1)(3b+1)(3b+2)/b², while delta/q=(b-1)/b; conjugacy gives an even analytic expansion and O(delta⁴) error. The verified standalone code independently expands symbolic identities and high-precision solves nonlinear equations for b=-4/5,-1/2,-1/5. The claim is local and does not assert infinite global orbit coverage, attractor existence or nonresonant Neimark-Sacker behavior at 1:3 and 1:4 resonances.

originality.rationale: Rech–Beims–Gallas 2004 derives the equal-drive analytic period-two spectral curve only and explicitly identifies mismatch as a follow-up. Rech–Beims–Gallas 2007 analyzes the same equal-drive symmetric map plus a different quadratic asymmetric-coupling map; neither contains opposite drive shifts a±delta or derives the second-order spectral-threshold coefficient. Lloyd 1995 uses post-map diffusive logistic coupling and gives numerical dynamical regimes, not this local unequal-drive coefficient. Published-result database queries and accessible own historical claims identified no identical result or dominating implication. The factorization and two exact sign reversals are not statements of the inspected prior theorems. Historical completeness and unindexed priority remain genuine risks.

value.rationale: The 2004 primary article explicitly proposes investigating parameter mismatch in an experimentally motivated pair of nonlinear oscillators. The exactly computable leading response of the period-two unit-circle boundary is a natural parameter-sensitivity invariant and changes sign twice at -2/3 and -1/3. This separates three robust qualitative response regimes with the same symmetric reference spectrum; it is not a normalization identity or routine substitution, since the four orbit equations and spectral determinant must be continued jointly. It supplies a sharp structural boundary despite not claiming the existence of a global attractor or invariant curve. The vanishing curvatures are precisely identified rather than inflated into unproved all-order cancellations.
